scope: Read-only authenticated document GET on deployed cloud-test data-plane; loopback HTTP; existing small record; no financial payloads retained

Short samples explain current latency, not a sustained workload qualification.

findings: Two serial durable side-effect writes dominate this read endpoint.
Slow flush acknowledgment on the QNAP-backed storage path accounts for most observed latency; the lookup/authorization/HTTP remainder is about 2 ms.
The previous full-scan accounting fix does not remove the durable-write latency floor.
Changing fsync to fdatasync alone did not materially improve the raw-file control.
recommendedNextWork: Inspect QNAP LUN backing pool, physical media, synchronous write/cache behavior and contention, or benchmark a suitable low-latency SSD/NVMe volume before migrating database storage.
Consider committing audit and quota admission together with preserved authorization, idempotency and crash semantics to reduce serial flushes.
Do not remove synchronous durability merely to improve reported latency.
